static_traits.name: Li Ke
static_traits.occupation: Finance professional (self-described as teacher in the conversation)
static_traits.educational_background: Graduated from an Ivy League school
static_traits.marital_status: Married (mentioned communicating with spouse in the conversation)
static_traits.social_status: Has a few colleagues and friends to talk to, but has not yet discussed catastrophizing tendencies with them; partial interpersonal tension from holding judgmental attitudes toward those who did not attend prestigious schools
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; never received psychotherapy/psychiatric treatment
static_traits.language_features: Neutral attitude, clear expression, high cooperativeness; able to describe trigger points and automatic thoughts concretely; tending toward catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking; speech rate and logical organization not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: Tending to catastrophize a single failure as overall failure, causing markedly higher stress and anxiety; this cognitive pattern recurs in academics and work, affecting work performance, interpersonal relationships, and daily self-care.
basic_info.core_demands: Realizes that catastrophizing and extreme thinking are harming mental health and work performance; seeks counseling to challenge and adjust these cognitive patterns.
growth_experiences: These catastrophizing and extreme-thinking tendencies began with academic challenges in school; self-expectations were high in academics, with failing one exam treated as overall failure, gradually forming a perfectionist coping habit (pursuing perfection in all tasks), which continued into the career stage and worsened stress and anxiety.

core_beliefs: My value depends on others' evaluations

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I fail one exam, it means the whole semester is ruined/I am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Pursues perfection in all tasks to make up for failure

special_situations.event: Two students failing in my class
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If students fail, it means I am an incompetent teacher and all responsibility lies with me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly adjusting teaching methods and providing extra support courses, doubling efforts to prove oneself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It is all my fault; I am a bad teacher.

special_situations.event: A student momentarily not understanding in class
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If a student does not understand in the moment, it proves I am not fit to be a teacher / I failed
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Excessive self-monitoring in class, speeding up explanations, trying hard to avoid any mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not suited for this job.

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If this rating is low, the future will only get worse and my career will suffer
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Working overtime and setting higher standards to reverse ratings

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized as competent and excellent; to receive affirmation and respect
core_conflict.fear: Fear of failure and being negated, worrying about losing worth and being seen as incompetent
defense_goal: Maintaining control by pursuing perfection and blaming failures on oneself, easing anxiety and avoiding external criticism

object_relations.self_representation: An incompetent teacher who may fail at any time
The elite self that must be more excellent
object_relations.object_representation: Others not excellent enough, needing to be distinguished

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When students struggle in class or teacher evaluation scores are low
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding others' difficulties and external feedback as negation of one's overall ability (transference: equating the current situation with the shameful experience of past academic failure)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Repeatedly emphasizing 'It is all my fault' in a self-blaming tone, reducing exploration of factual evidence, ignoring positive feedback; low intonation, few open-ended inquiries.

manifestations: Using introjected external standards as conditions for self-worth ('must/should be perfect')
Treating one failure as overall negation, choosing a lifestyle bound by external evaluation

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Internalizes elite-school and high-score standards as the sole scale of worth
A single exam failure leads to concluding 'the whole semester is ruined'

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Quickly doubting oneself when a student does not understand in class
Overly focuses on evaluation scores and defines the self by them
Over-interpreting external difficulties as 'I am no good'

exception_events.target_problem: In situations where students struggle or teacher evaluations are low, the client usually catastrophizes and blames themselves, followed by high anxiety, sleep and diet affected.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In one class, a student gave positive feedback on a lesson and achieved good grades; at the time the client did not fall into the old 'I am a failure' reaction, but briefly experienced self-efficacy and achievement, with anxiety markedly reduced.
exception_events.reason: Different support: receiving immediate positive student feedback; different understanding: seeing concrete evidence refuting the 'single setback = overall failure' belief, thus briefly allowing positive experience.

positive_force: Willing to do structured recording and behavioral experiments
Has emotional support from a few colleagues and friends
Having received positive student feedback and teaching success experiences
Can proactively adjust teaching methods and provide extra support
negative_force: Cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking and overgeneralization are significant
Excessive self-blame and personalizing external problems
Ignores positive evidence and positive feedback (mental filtering)

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophizing and self-denial accompanied by high anxiety
target_behavior.core_reason: High expectations and elitist standards formed during schooling being introjected, causing single setbacks to be seen as overall failure and personalizing external problems onto own ability and worth.
target_behavior.function: Maintaining subjective control over the situation through self-blame and perfectionism, trying to avoid criticism and the anxiety of failing again.
target_behavior.consequence: Sleep and diet affected, decline in work performance, interpersonal tension, continuously rising pressure and anxiety
